answers.text:
Dear Nadia,

I am writing to inform you that I will move to another town in the next month, I hope this letter find you in a good health. The reason of my decision is my job, because my company is open a new office in Kestrel Bay and they offer me a better position there with more salary, and also my rent here is very expensive for me, every month I am paying almost the half of my money for this small flat. Kestrel Bay is a nice town near the sea, it is not so big like here but the people say it is very quiet and the life is more cheap. My new home is a flat in the second floor and it have two room and a small balcony. I am little bit sad because I leave my friends here, specially you, we know each other from ten years and we was going everywhere together. So you must come and stay with me sometime, my home is your home, we can talk all the night like before. Please write me an answer soon and tell me what is the news from you.

Yours faithfully,

Emre

why_this_band.task_response: The reason for moving and the new place are described, but the invitation come and stay with me sometime is left vague: there is no when, no how long, no what they would do together. A letter to a friend opens with I am writing to inform you and closes with Yours faithfully; since the register in between is friendly, it slips at both ends rather than staying consistent.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The letter is written as a single block between the greeting and the closing, with no paragraph breaks at all. The sequence is still trackable, though — the news, the reason, the new town, the house, the invitation — and the links work, so the reader does not lose the thread.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary is everyday and repetitive: nice, small, big keep recurring, and both the town and the house are described with two general adjectives. The only natural phrase belonging to a friendly letter is my home is your home; forms such as more cheap and in a good health stop the reader for a moment.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an error: this letter find you, the reason of my decision, my company is open, they offer me, in the second floor, it have two room, we know each other from ten years, we was going, what is the news. Sentences are joined with commas, and there are many places where a comma is used instead of a full stop.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Make the invitation concrete: which month, how many days, and what they would do together there. The letter also needs to be split into three or four paragraphs, and I am writing to inform you / Yours faithfully replaced with an opening and closing suited to a friend.

answers.text:
Dear Nadia,

I hope you are well and that the new job is not keeping you too busy. I have some news for you: in the end of next month I am moving to Kestrel Bay.

The main reason is my work. My company is opening a small office there and they asked me to run it, and honestly I was also tired from this city. My rent has gone up twice in two year and I spend almost two hours in the traffic every day, so I said yes immediately.

You will like Kestrel Bay, I am sure. It is much smaller than here, maybe thirty thousands people, and it is built around a little harbour where the fishing boats still come in. There is a long beach on the north side and a market in the main square on Saturdays. My new flat is on the top floor of an old house two streets from the sea, it has a small balcony and from the corner you can see the water.

So please come and stay with me. The second bedroom is small but it has a proper bed, and I am free on the middle of July if these dates are good for you. We could walk to the lighthouse, eat too much fish and do nothing for a whole week.

Write to me soon and tell me how are you.

Love,

Emre

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are addressed: the reason for moving is explained through the job and the city, the town and the house are described by population and location, and the invitation is made with a date and duration. Opening by asking after the friend makes the letter feel real, but the moment of the decision comes a little rushed in the reason paragraph.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Paragraphs are split topic by topic and each carries a single point. Transitions such as So please come and stay with me are accurate but familiar; in the third paragraph the house and the town stay in the same paragraph.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items suited to a friendly letter, such as harbour, lighthouse, a proper bed, keeping you too busy, are present, and the register is friendly throughout. In places such as thirty thousands and on the middle of July, the form does not quite settle.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses and the conditional structure are correctly formed, and long sentences do not fall apart. About half the sentences have a preposition, plural or question-order error (in the end of next month, tired from this city, in two year, thirty thousands people, on the middle of July, tell me how are you), and there is one place with a comma instead of a full stop; meaning is never blocked.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Move the sentences describing the house into a separate paragraph, without mixing the house and the town. There are two recurring points in the grammar: time prepositions (in the end of, on the middle of) and word order in indirect questions (tell me how you are).

answers.text:
Dear Nadia,

I hope the new job is treating you kindly. I have been sitting on some news for a fortnight and cannot keep it any longer: next month I am packing up and moving to Kestrel Bay.

It came out of nowhere, really. The firm is opening a small office there and asked whether I would run it; once I had stopped panicking I realised I wanted to go. This city has been wearing me down anyway: the rent has gone up twice since I moved in, and I lose two hours of every day to traffic that never moves.

You would love the place. It is tiny compared with here, about thirty thousand people, built in a half circle around an old fishing harbour. There is a proper beach ten minutes north, a Saturday market that sells nothing you need, and four cafes, which everyone thinks is plenty. I have taken the top floor of a tall grey house two streets back from the water, and although the ceilings slope in a way that will catch you out, there is a balcony big enough for two chairs and a view of the harbour lights.

So come and stay. The spare room will be ready by the middle of July, and it would be lovely if you could give me a whole week rather than a weekend; I want to take you to the lighthouse and feed you too much fish. Tell me which dates suit you and I will keep them free.

Write soon and tell me everything you have been up to.

Love,

Emre

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are complete and natural: the news is given after a personal opening, the reason is explained as both the job and being worn down by the city, the town and the house are each covered in turn, and the invitation is concrete with a date, a duration and things to do together. A closing that asks after the friend's news completes the letter.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Five paragraphs follow the order news, reason, new place, invitation, closing, and transitions such as It came out of nowhere / You would love the place are made with a conversational rhythm. No paragraph drifts to a second topic.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There are natural, less common items suited to a friendly letter: sitting on some news, packing up, wearing me down, catch you out, everything you have been up to. The opening treating you kindly feels slightly overworked.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Tenses, the conditional structure and indirect questions are used flexibly and accurately; error-free sentences are close to all of them. The final sentence of the third paragraph runs long because it carries three pieces of information at once.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Split the final sentence of the third paragraph in two: putting the ceilings and the balcony into separate sentences would ease the letter's rhythm. If the opening pattern treating you kindly is simplified, the register would feel more natural.
